observations.title: The recurrence is broken in practice but not codified, so the risk returns at v6
observations.detail: My v4 O-1 recommended a standing rule requiring the immediately preceding generation's pins to be added complete with advisory roster in the same edit. honestyRepairsFromV4[0] books it as 'Substance of O-1 is this pinChainRule repair', and the instance is genuinely fixed - claude2v4 is enumerated. But pinChainRule's text is byte-identical to v4's: 'Each successor pins the verdicts it folds. Every pin record enumerates the full blocker, shouldFix, and advisory roster of the file it pins.' No standing rule was added. Not a finding: O-1 was advisory, I framed it as a recommendation to the coordinator rather than an obligation on the author, and this successor discharged it by doing the right thing. Recorded so the coordinator knows the structural guard still does not exist and v6 depends on the author repeating the behaviour.

observations.title: The empty-newest-pin pattern is broken for the first time in four generations
observations.detail: v3 repaired claude2v1 and left claude2v2 empty; v4 repaired claude2v2 and left claude2v3 empty; v5 repairs claude2v3 AND enumerates claude2v4 in the same edit. I recomputed all four rosters from the frozen verdicts by severity rather than reading the subject's claims: claude2v1 ['O-1','O-2'], claude2v2 ['O-1'], claude2v3 ['O-1','O-2','O-3'], claude2v4 ['O-1','O-2','O-3'] - every one matches, each with an observationsNote naming the RESOLVED-NOTED exclusion. This is what CLAUDE-V4-S1 asked for and one generation more than it asked for.

observations.title: The historical cosmetic slips are left untouched, and that is the correct call
observations.detail: reMeasurementAtV2.note still reads 'HISTORICAL HISTORICAL-AT-V2' (my v4 O-3). honestyRepairsFromV4[2] states plainly that those HISTORICAL notes are left untouched and not rewritten this generation, and the dispatch says the same. Correct: /reMeasurementAtV2 is not on v5's roster, so editing it would itself have been an off-roster change. Declining to fix a cosmetic slip rather than breaking the roster to reach it is the right trade, and saying so out loud is better than silently leaving it.

summary: I attacked every surface the dispatch and the artifact's own reviewGuidance name and found no blocker and no SHOULD-FIX. The finding I filed at v4 is repaired and then some: claude2v3 now enumerates its three advisories with an observationsNote, and claude2v4 is enumerated in the same edit instead of being left empty - breaking, for the first time in four generations, the pattern where each successor fixed the pin its reviewer named and emptied the newest one. I recomputed all four advisory rosters from my frozen verdicts by severity field rather than reading the subject's claims, and every pin matches exactly. Everything else re-measures clean: the roster is exact with zero off-roster paths, reviewGuidance is a pure append with no duplicates, exactly one field claims standing LIVE, and reMeasurementAtV5 genuinely measures the D-117 state - its COORD digest reproduces from git at the head it names, that head is live HEAD, and it is distinct from the V4 block. All carries remain byte-exact including the disclosed mid-sentence boundary, the DR-109 row reproduces at line 291, the ID-DEP-S5 status tokens re-measure correct, no commit/CAS/ledger API is invented, and no D-096 (A) grant or SATISFIED claim appears anywhere. Two judgement calls I want on the record. The historical cosmetic slips I raised at v4 are deliberately left untouched, and that is right - those blocks are not on this roster, so reaching them would have been an off-roster change; declining the fix and saying so beats breaking the roster to reach it. And my v4 O-1 asked for a codified standing rule against the recurrence; the instance is fixed but pinChainRule's text is unchanged, so the structural guard still does not exist. That was an advisory rather than an obligation, so it does not bear on the verdict, but v6 depends on the author repeating the behaviour rather than on a rule enforcing it.
